title: tsdk: runtime shape-index + deferred tag resolution for streaming polymorphic output
creator: Avery Kim
description: Build a small runtime 'shape-index' and a deferred tag-resolution flow to reliably map streaming responses to TypeScript union variants and Zod/JSON-Schema validators. Goal is to improve structured-output ergonomics for progressive/streaming parses where the discriminator (tag) appears late or is inferred from structure, without blowing up memory or latency.
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes a runtime ShapeIndex that can be populated from typegen metadata and consulted during streaming parse
Streaming parser supports deferred-tag-resolution: ability to buffer a small subtree until a tag is seen or fallback to structure-matching heuristics
Provides opt-in Zod and JSON-Schema adapter helpers that accept partials and run progressive validation during streaming
Benchmarks show <5% p99 latency regression for 512-token streams on typical client configs and <10% memory overhead for typical model responses
Unit + integration tests for edge cases (missing tag, tag as nested field, conflicting hints) with >=95% deterministic resolution in our test corpus
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Kickoff meeting with SDK, runtime, and product. Agreed scope: runtime-only shape index + streaming parse API changes; no immediate breaking surface for existing sync APIs.
2025-02-14: Prototyped ShapeIndex: compact fingerprint map (string -> variant key) generated from typegen metadata. Initial in-memory layout ~120 bytes/variant.
2025-02-16: Implemented deferred buffer in streaming parser; now buffers per-object up to configurable limit (default 2KB) while waiting for tag field. Emits fallback event if limit exceeded.
2025-02-18: Integrated Zod progressive adapter: can run partial checks as fields arrive and report early validation hints to caller. Added initial examples in examples/streaming-shape-hints.ts.
2025-02-20: Internal review with Runtime team. Requested: clearer metrics (cache hit/miss, buffer aborts), and an opt-out path for low-memory clients. Addressing comments now.
decisions: Use a compact runtime ShapeIndex generated at build-time from typegen metadata (fingerprint = set of characteristic field names + small hash of literal values). Avoid full JSON-Schema matching in hot path.
Deferred tag resolution implemented by buffering a limited subtree; default buffer cap 2KB to protect clients from unbounded buffering. Buffer cap configurable per-request.

Zod adapters will be provided as 'progressive' helpers that accept partial objects and return either 'inconclusive' | 'valid' | 'invalid' states, with the final validation executed when object is complete.
Fallback matching order: 1) explicit tag (fast path via ShapeIndex), 2) shape-fingerprint match, 3) last-resort structural scoring (best-effort with tie-breaker to first-registered variant).
No breaking changes to existing tsdk sync typegen surface. Streaming parser additions are opt-in under new parseStreamingWithHints API.
Runtime team asked to keep ShapeIndex serialization compact and stable across minor versions; we'll include a version header and migration notes in typegen output.
notes: Edge-case: models that encode tag as natural language ("as a string in content") are not resolved by ShapeIndex; will add a heuristic normalizer but mark as low-confidence.
We need to be careful with cached ShapeIndex across different tenants; include tenant scoping if customers opt into private model registries.
Follow-up: export telemetry for buffer aborts, fallback hits, and zod progressive failures so Product can quantify customer-facing regressions.
Open question: Should we expose a developer hook to provide custom matching functions? (Product leans yes; runtime concerned about safety).
